subject: history_social
passage: Along the coast of Kerala, India, fishers sell their catch at beach markets. Before the late 1990s, a boat usually landed at its nearest market, so on the same day fish could be very expensive at one market and very cheap at another. Economist Arjun Menon argues that mobile phones made prices more even, because fishers still at sea could call several markets and then sail to the one paying the most.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Menon's argument?

choices.A: After mobile phones arrived, nearly every boat still landed at its nearest market, just as before.
choices.B: Before mobile phones arrived, some markets sold fish caught by boats from several different villages.
choices.C: After mobile phones arrived, many fishers also began using them to talk with their families while at sea.
choices.D: After mobile phones arrived, boats often sailed past their nearest market to sell at one paying more.

explanation.why: Menon's explanation depends on a change in behavior: with phones, fishers chose the best-paying market instead of the nearest one. A finding that boats really did start sailing past their nearest market to sell elsewhere supports that explanation.
explanation.A: Incorrect. If boats kept landing at the nearest market, phones did not change where fish were sold, so this would weaken the argument.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This describes markets before phones and says nothing about how phones changed prices.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Calling family members does not show that phones changed where fishers sold their catch.
explanation.D: Correct. This shows fishers using information to choose the higher-paying market, which is exactly how Menon says prices became more even.
